reasoning: The claim is scientifically accurate and widely accepted. Data collected over decades by the Lunar Laser Ranging experiment—which bounces lasers off retroreflectors left on the lunar surface by the Apollo and Luna missions—precisely measures the rate at which the Moon is receding from Earth at approximately 3.8 centimeters (1.5 inches) per year. This recession is caused by tidal friction. Earth's rotation drags the tidal bulges ahead of the Moon's orbital position, transferring rotational angular momentum from Earth to the Moon's orbit, which gradually pushes the Moon into a higher, larger orbit.
